chapter_text:
CHAPTER 1 — सुभाषितानि (SUBHASHITANI)

Introduction — सुभाषितम् किम्?

The word सुभाषितम् (subhashitam) is formed from सु (su = well, good) + भाषितम् (bhashitam = that which is spoken). A सुभाषितम् is therefore a "well-said saying" — a short, memorable Sanskrit verse (usually a single श्लोक of two lines) that packs a piece of worldly wisdom, moral teaching, or ethical insight into a beautifully composed form. For centuries these verses have been recited by teachers, parents and elders across India to teach values in a way that is easy to remember and pleasant to hear. In this lesson (NIOS Secondary Sanskrit, Course 209) we read ten famous public-domain subhashitas, learn their word meanings (शब्दार्थ), translate them into simple English, draw out their morals, and use them to learn a little Sanskrit grammar (व्याकरणम्).

Why subhashitas matter (सुभाषितानां महत्त्वम्)

Sanskrit literature is enormously rich in गद्य (prose) and पद्य (verse). Among verses, subhashitas occupy a special place because they are compact, rhythmic and full of meaning. A good subhashita does three things at once: it delights the ear (सुन्दरता), it sharpens the intellect (बुद्धिः), and it improves character (सदाचारः). The famous line "सुभाषितं हि गङ्गाया अपि पावनम्" reminds us that a good saying can purify the mind even more than a holy river. Because they are easy to memorise, subhashitas were the everyday "textbook of values" long before printed books existed. Even today they help a student learn vocabulary, sandhi and grammar naturally, while absorbing timeless lessons about hard work, truthfulness, humility and compassion.

Ten famous subhashitas (शब्दार्थ सहित)

1) विद्या ददाति विनयं विनयाद्याति पात्रताम् ।
   पात्रत्वात् धनमाप्नोति धनात् धर्मं ततः सुखम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: विद्या = knowledge; ददाति = gives; विनयम् = humility, good conduct; विनयात् = from humility; याति = attains, goes to; पात्रताम् = worthiness, fitness; पात्रत्वात् = from worthiness; धनम् = wealth; आप्नोति = obtains; धनात् = from wealth; धर्मम् = righteous conduct, duty; ततः = thence, from that; सुखम् = happiness.
   Translation: Knowledge gives humility; from humility one gains worthiness; from worthiness one obtains wealth; from wealth (one performs) righteous duty, and from that (comes) happiness.
   Theme / Moral: True education is a ladder — it begins with humility and ends in happiness. Knowledge that does not make us humble is incomplete.

2) उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः ।
   न हि सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य प्रविशन्ति मुखे मृगाः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: उद्यमेन = by effort, industry; हि = indeed; सिध्यन्ति = are accomplished; कार्याणि = tasks, works; न = not; मनोरथैः = by (mere) wishes, day-dreams; सुप्तस्य = of the sleeping; सिंहस्य = of the lion; प्रविशन्ति = enter; मुखे = into the mouth; मृगाः = deer, animals.
   Translation: Tasks are accomplished by effort, not by mere wishes; indeed, deer do not walk into the mouth of a sleeping lion.
   Theme / Moral: Hard work, not day-dreaming, brings success. Even the mighty lion must hunt.

3) काकः कृष्णः पिकः कृष्णः को भेदः पिककाकयोः ।
   वसन्तसमये प्राप्ते काकः काकः पिकः पिकः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: काकः = crow; कृष्णः = black; पिकः = cuckoo (koel); कः = what; भेदः = difference; पिककाकयोः = between the koel and the crow; वसन्तसमये = in the spring season; प्राप्ते = when arrived; काकः काकः = a crow (remains) a crow; पिकः पिकः = a koel (remains) a koel.
   Translation: The crow is black, the koel is black — what is the difference between koel and crow? But when spring arrives, the crow is (shown to be) a crow and the koel a koel.
   Theme / Moral: Outward appearances may look alike; true worth is revealed only at the right time (the koel's sweet song in spring).

4) अयं निजः परो वेति गणना लघुचेतसाम् ।
   उदारचरितानां तु वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: अयम् = this (person); निजः = one's own; परः = other, stranger; वा = or; इति = thus; गणना = calculation, reckoning; लघुचेतसाम् = of the narrow-minded; उदारचरितानाम् = of the noble-hearted; तु = but; वसुधा = the earth; एव = indeed; कुटुम्बकम् = family.
   Translation: "This one is my own, that one a stranger" — such is the reckoning of the narrow-minded. But for the noble-hearted, the whole earth is (one) family.
   Theme / Moral: वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम् — the noble see all humanity as one family; only small minds divide people into "mine" and "other".

5) सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात् न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम् ।
   प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात् एष धर्मः सनातनः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: सत्यम् = truth; ब्रूयात् = one should speak; प्रियम् = pleasant, agreeable; न = not; अप्रियम् = unpleasant; च = and; अनृतम् = falsehood, untruth; एषः = this; धर्मः = eternal law, duty; सनातनः = eternal, ancient.
   Translation: Speak the truth, speak what is pleasant; do not speak an unpleasant truth; and do not speak a pleasant falsehood — this is the eternal law.
   Theme / Moral: Balance truth with kindness. Truth should be spoken gently; pleasantness must never become a lie.

6) पुस्तकस्था तु या विद्या परहस्तगतं धनम् ।
   कार्यकाले समुत्पन्ने न सा विद्या न तद्धनम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: पुस्तकस्था = remaining (only) in the book; तु = but; या = which; विद्या = knowledge; परहस्तगतम् = gone into another's hand; धनम् = wealth; कार्यकाले = at the time of need/work; समुत्पन्ने = having arisen; न सा विद्या = that knowledge is (of) no (use); न तत् धनम् = nor that wealth.
   Translation: Knowledge that stays (only) in the book and wealth that has passed into another's hand — when the time of need arises, that knowledge is no knowledge and that wealth is no wealth.
   Theme / Moral: Learning must be practised and remembered, not merely stored in books; useful knowledge is knowledge we can actually apply.

7) उदये सविता रक्तो रक्तश्चास्तमये तथा ।
   सम्पत्तौ च विपत्तौ च महतामेकरूपता ॥
   शब्दार्थ: उदये = at rising; सविता = the sun; रक्तः = red; अस्तमये = at setting; तथा = likewise; सम्पत्तौ = in prosperity; विपत्तौ = in adversity; महताम् = of the great; एकरूपता = sameness, evenness (of temper).
   Translation: The sun is red at its rising and red likewise at its setting; in prosperity and in adversity, great souls remain the same.
   Theme / Moral: Great people keep an even mind in good times and bad — steadiness of character, like the constant sun.

8) आलस्यं हि मनुष्याणां शरीरस्थो महान् रिपुः ।
   नास्त्युद्यमसमो बन्धुः कृत्वा यं नावसीदति ॥
   शब्दार्थ: आलस्यम् = laziness; हि = indeed; मनुष्याणाम् = of men; शरीरस्थः = residing in the body; महान् = great; रिपुः = enemy; नास्ति = there is not; उद्यमसमः = equal to industry/effort; बन्धुः = friend, kinsman; कृत्वा = having done/cultivated; यम् = which; न अवसीदति = one does not sink, decline.
   Translation: Laziness is indeed a great enemy dwelling within the body of men; there is no friend like industry, cultivating which one never sinks (into ruin).
   Theme / Moral: Laziness is our inner enemy; diligence is our truest friend.

9) परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः परोपकाराय वहन्ति नद्यः ।
   परोपकाराय दुहन्ति गावः परोपकारार्थमिदं शरीरम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: परोपकाराय = for the good of others; फलन्ति = bear fruit; वृक्षाः = trees; वहन्ति = flow; नद्यः = rivers; दुहन्ति = yield (milk); गावः = cows; परोपकारार्थम् = for the purpose of helping others; इदम् = this; शरीरम् = body.
   Translation: Trees bear fruit for others, rivers flow for others, cows give milk for others — this body too is (meant) for helping others.
   Theme / Moral: परोपकार (service to others) is the very purpose of life; nature itself lives for the benefit of others.

10) क्षणशः कणशश्चैव विद्यामर्थं च साधयेत् ।
    क्षणे नष्टे कुतो विद्या कणे नष्टे कुतो धनम् ॥
    शब्दार्थ: क्षणशः = moment by moment; कणशः = particle by particle; च = and; एव = indeed; विद्याम् = knowledge; अर्थम् = wealth; साधयेत् = one should acquire; क्षणे = when a moment; नष्टे = is lost; कुतः = whence, how; विद्या = knowledge; कणे = when a particle; धनम् = wealth.
   Translation: One should gather knowledge moment by moment and wealth particle by particle; if a moment is wasted, how can there be knowledge? If a particle is lost, how can there be wealth?
   Theme / Moral: Do not waste time or resources; small, steady efforts build great learning and prosperity.

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar from the verses (English explanation, Devanagari examples)

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — the joining of sounds). When two sounds meet in Sanskrit, they often combine and change. The commonest kind here is दीर्घ-सन्धि (long-vowel sandhi): when a short vowel meets a similar vowel, the two merge into a single long vowel. Examples drawn from our verses:
  • विद्या + अर्थी → विद्यार्थी (आ + अ = आ) — "student".
  • विनयात् + याति → विनयाद्याति (त् before य softens to द् — व्यञ्जन-सन्धि). Split it back as विनयात् + याति.
  • वसुधा + एव → वसुधैव (आ + ए = ऐ, गुण/वृद्धि-सन्धि) — "the earth alone".
  • न + अस्ति → नास्ति (अ + अ = आ) — "there is not"; न + अवसीदति → नावसीदति.
  • धनम् + आप्नोति → धनमाप्नोति (म् + आ; the anusvāra/म् joins). Split as धनम् + आप्नोति.
  • कणशः + च + एव → कणशश्चैव (visarga ः before च becomes श्; च + एव → चैव).
Being able to SPLIT a sandhi (सन्धि-विच्छेद) back into its parts is a key reading skill.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). Sanskrit nouns change their ending to show their role in the sentence. Using the masculine a-stem राम as a model:
  • प्रथमा (nominative, "the subject"): रामः — used for the doer. In our verses सविता (nom.) "the sun", वृक्षाः (nom. plural) "trees".
  • द्वितीया (accusative, "the object"): रामम् — used for what is acted upon. विनयम्, विद्याम्, अर्थम् are objects ("gives HUMILITY", "acquire KNOWLEDGE").
  • तृतीया (instrumental, "by/with"): रामेण — the means. उद्यमेन "BY effort", मनोरथैः "BY wishes" (plural).
  • पञ्चमी (ablative, "from"): रामात् — the source. विनयात् "FROM humility", धनात् "FROM wealth", पात्रत्वात् "FROM worthiness".
  • षष्ठी (genitive, "of"): रामस्य — possession. सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य "of the sleeping lion", मनुष्याणाम् "of men" (plural), महताम् "of the great".
  • सप्तमी (locative, "in/at/on"): रामे — place or time. मुखे "in the mouth", वसन्तसमये "in spring", सम्पत्तौ "in prosperity", कार्यकाले "at the time of work".

(C) शब्दरूप (declension of a noun — worked example). The word राम (masculine, ending in अ) declines through the three numbers as follows for the first case (प्रथमा): एकवचन रामः (one), द्विवचन रामौ (two), बहुवचन रामाः (many). Notice how in the verses काकः (crow) and पिकः (koel) are singular nominatives ending in -ः, while वृक्षाः (trees), नद्यः (rivers) and गावः (cows) are plural nominatives — telling us "many" of each. Similarly the feminine word विद्या (in विद्या ददाति) is प्रथमा एकवचन, the subject "knowledge".

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you learned that a सुभाषितम् is a "well-spoken" verse carrying wisdom in a compact, memorable form, and that such verses have long been India's everyday teaching of values. You read ten famous public-domain subhashitas — on the value of humility-through-knowledge, the necessity of effort over day-dreaming, the difference between real and apparent worth, universal brotherhood (वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम्), speaking truth kindly, the uselessness of unused knowledge, the even mind of great souls, laziness as the inner enemy, service to others (परोपकार), and the steady gathering of learning and wealth. For each you studied the शब्दार्थ (word meanings), an English translation, and the moral. Finally you drew grammar from the verses: दीर्घ- and other सन्धि (and how to split them), the six common विभक्ति case-endings with examples, and a शब्दरूप model (रामः / रामौ / रामाः). Memorise a few of these verses — they will enrich both your Sanskrit and your character.

topics.name: सुभाषितम् — Meaning and Importance of Subhashitas
topics.description: What a सुभाषितम् (su + bhashitam, 'well-said saying') is; its form as a short memorable श्लोक; and why subhashitas have long served as India's everyday teaching of values, vocabulary and grammar.

topics.name: Selected Subhashitas and their Meanings
topics.description: Ten famous public-domain subhashitas presented with their verse, meaning and context — from 'विद्या ददाति विनयम्' to 'परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः' — and how to read and recite them.

topics.name: शब्दार्थ — Word Meanings and Vocabulary
topics.description: Building Sanskrit vocabulary through word-by-word शब्दार्थ of each verse: nouns, verbs and case-forms such as उद्यमेन, विनयात्, मनोरथैः, वसुधा, परोपकाराय and their English meanings.

topics.name: Moral and Ethical Themes
topics.description: The moral and ethical themes carried by the verses — humility, hard work, truthfulness with kindness, universal brotherhood, service to others, steadiness of mind and the danger of laziness.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Verses (Sandhi and Vibhakti)
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the verses: दीर्घ and other सन्धि with सन्धि-विच्छेद (splitting), the six common विभक्ति case endings (प्रथमा to सप्तमी) with examples, and a शब्दरूप model of the a-stem noun राम.

topics.name: Translation and Comprehension
topics.description: Translating verses into simple English and answering comprehension questions — identifying the subject, object, key word meanings and the moral of a given subhashita.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: सुभाषितम् — Meaning and Importance of Subhashitas
learning_outcomes.description: Explain what a सुभाषितम् is (सु + भाषितम्) and describe why subhashitas are important in Sanskrit literature and in everyday moral learning.
Recall and recite selected famous subhashitas and identify each verse by its opening words and central idea.
Explain the meaning of a given subhashita as a whole and relate its imagery (lion, crow, sun, trees) to its message.
Give the शब्दार्थ (word meaning) in English of Sanskrit words drawn from the verses and use the vocabulary correctly.
Analyse the moral or ethical theme of a subhashita and apply its lesson to everyday situations.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Verses (Sandhi and Vibhakti)
learning_outcomes.description: Identify and perform simple सन्धि joins and splits (सन्धि-विच्छेद) using examples taken from the verses.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Verses (Sandhi and Vibhakti)
learning_outcomes.description: Recognise the six common विभक्ति case endings and the शब्दरूप of an a-stem noun, and state the case/role of a word in a verse.
Translate a given subhashita into simple English and answer comprehension questions about its words, grammar and moral.

chapter_summary.title: सुभाषितानि (Subhashitani) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Secondary Sanskrit (209) summary for Chapter 1. It explains what a सुभाषितम् (well-said verse) is and why such verses matter, presents ten famous public-domain subhashitas with their meanings and morals, and draws simple grammar — सन्धि and विभक्ति — from the verses.

sections.heading: What a subhashita is and why it matters
bullets: सुभाषितम् = सु (good/well) + भाषितम् (spoken): a well-said verse, usually a two-line श्लोक, that carries a moral or worldly wisdom.
Subhashitas delight the ear, sharpen the intellect and improve character — they were the everyday 'textbook of values' before printed books.
Because they are short and rhythmic they are easy to memorise, and they teach vocabulary, सन्धि and grammar naturally.

sections.heading: Verses on knowledge, effort and time
bullets: विद्या ददाति विनयम्: knowledge gives humility, leading step by step to worthiness, wealth, righteousness and happiness.
उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः: tasks are achieved by effort, not wishes — deer do not enter a sleeping lion's mouth.
पुस्तकस्था तु या विद्या...: knowledge left only in books (and wealth in another's hand) is useless in the hour of need.
क्षणशः कणशश्चैव...: gather knowledge moment by moment and wealth particle by particle; waste nothing.

sections.heading: Verses on character and values
bullets: अयं निजः परो वेति...: only the narrow-minded divide people into 'mine' and 'other'; for the noble, वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम् — the world is one family.
सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात्...: speak the truth, and speak kindly; never an unpleasant truth nor a pleasant lie.
उदये सविता रक्तः...: like the constant sun, great souls keep an even mind in prosperity and adversity.
परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः...: trees, rivers and cows live for others — so should this body (परोपकार).

sections.heading: Sandhi from the verses
bullets: दीर्घ-सन्धि: a short vowel + a similar vowel merge into one long vowel — विद्या + अर्थी = विद्यार्थी (आ+अ=आ), न + अस्ति = नास्ति.
वृद्धि-सन्धि: वसुधा + एव = वसुधैव (आ + ए = ऐ).
व्यञ्जन/विसर्ग-सन्धि: विनयात् + याति = विनयाद्याति; कणशः + च = कणशश्च.
सन्धि-विच्छेद (splitting a joined form back into its parts) is a key reading skill.

sections.heading: Vibhakti and shabda-rupa
bullets: प्रथमा (nominative, subject): रामः; in the verses सविता, वृक्षाः, काकः.
द्वितीया (accusative, object): रामम्; in the verses विनयम्, विद्याम्, अर्थम्.
तृतीया 'by' रामेण/उद्यमेन; पञ्चमी 'from' रामात्/विनयात्; षष्ठी 'of' रामस्य/सिंहस्य; सप्तमी 'in' रामे/मुखे.
शब्दरूप of a-stem राम (प्रथमा): एकवचन रामः, द्विवचन रामौ, बहुवचन रामाः.

key_takeaways: A सुभाषितम् (सु + भाषितम्) is a well-said verse that teaches wisdom in a short, memorable form.
Effort, not day-dreaming, brings success — उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः.
True knowledge begins with humility (विद्या ददाति विनयम्) and must be used, not merely stored in books.
The noble see the whole world as one family — वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम्; and life's purpose is परोपकार (service to others).
Speak the truth, but speak it kindly — सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात्.
दीर्घ-सन्धि merges a short vowel with a similar vowel into one long vowel (न + अस्ति = नास्ति); splitting it is सन्धि-विच्छेद.
विभक्ति endings show a word's role: प्रथमा subject, द्वितीया object, तृतीया by, पञ्चमी from, षष्ठी of, सप्तमी in.

glossary.definition: A 'well-said' verse (सु + भाषितम्); a short Sanskrit श्लोक carrying moral or worldly wisdom in a memorable form.
A verse or stanza, usually of two lines (four quarters/पाद), the common form in which subhashitas are composed.
The word-meaning; the English (or simple) meaning of each Sanskrit word in a verse.
Knowledge or learning; in the verses the source of humility, worthiness and ultimately happiness.
Humility, modesty, good conduct — the first gift of true knowledge.
Effort, industry, diligence; by उद्यम tasks are accomplished (उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि).
A wish or day-dream; contrasted with real effort in the verse उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति...
Service to, or the good of, others; the theme of 'परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः' and a central Sanskrit value.
'The whole earth is one family' — the noble-hearted view that all humanity is one, from अयं निजः परो वेति...
Eternal, ancient, everlasting; used of the eternal law (धर्मः सनातनः) of speaking truth kindly.
The joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; e.g. दीर्घ-सन्धि merges a short vowel with a like vowel into a long one.
The splitting of a sandhi form back into its separate words, e.g. नास्ति = न + अस्ति.
A noun's case ending, showing its role: प्रथमा (subject), द्वितीया (object), तृतीया (by), पञ्चमी (from), षष्ठी (of), सप्तमी (in).
The full declension of a noun through cases and numbers, e.g. राम: रामः / रामौ / रामाः in the nominative.
Righteous conduct, duty or moral law; the goal reached through knowledge, worthiness and wealth in verse 1.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — सुभाषितानि (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 1)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the verses in the lesson where needed.

questions.question:
Translate the following subhashita into simple English:
उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः ।
न हि सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य प्रविशन्ति मुखे मृगाः ॥
questions.answer: Tasks/works are accomplished by effort (उद्यम), not by mere wishes or day-dreams (मनोरथ). Indeed, deer (मृगाः) do not walk into the mouth (मुखे) of a sleeping lion (सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य) — even the powerful lion must make an effort to eat.
questions.explanation: Effort brings success; the sleeping-lion image shows that nothing comes without action.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: विद्या, विनयम्, धनम्, सुखम्, ददाति.
questions.answer: विद्या = knowledge/learning; विनयम् = humility (accusative, 'humility' as object); धनम् = wealth; सुखम् = happiness; ददाति = (it) gives.
questions.explanation: These words come from verse 1: विद्या ददाति विनयम्...

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain the moral of 'सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात् न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम्'.
questions.answer: One should always speak the truth, but speak it in a pleasant, kind way. One must not speak a harsh/unpleasant truth (nor a pleasant lie). The moral is to balance truthfulness with kindness.
questions.explanation: The verse teaches truthful yet considerate speech as the सनातन (eternal) dharma.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) नास्ति (b) वसुधैव.
questions.answer: (a) नास्ति = न + अस्ति (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि). (b) वसुधैव = वसुधा + एव (आ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धि-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form back into its words is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its meaning-role for each underlined word: उद्यमेन, विनयात्, मुखे.
questions.answer: उद्यमेन = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'by effort'. विनयात् = पञ्चमी (ablative) → 'from humility'. मुखे = सप्तमी (locative) → 'in the mouth'.
questions.explanation: तृतीया shows means, पञ्चमी shows source, सप्तमी shows place.

questions.question: Explain the theme 'वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम्' using the verse 'अयं निजः परो वेति गणना लघुचेतसाम्, उदारचरितानां तु वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम्'. How can a student practise this idea today?
questions.answer:
The verse contrasts two kinds of people. The narrow-minded (लघुचेतस्) keep counting 'this person is my own (निजः), that one is a stranger (परः)'. But the noble-hearted (उदारचरित) do not divide people this way — for them the whole earth (वसुधा) itself is one family (कुटुम्बकम्). The theme वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम् teaches universal brotherhood: all human beings are one family, deserving kindness and respect regardless of nation, religion or background.
A student can practise this by helping classmates without discriminating, being kind to strangers and people from other places, sharing and cooperating, respecting other cultures, and thinking of the welfare of all rather than only 'my own' group. This broadens the heart from selfishness (लघुचेतस्) to generosity (उदारचरित).
questions.explanation: Contrast लघुचेतस् vs उदारचरित; explain universal brotherhood and give practical applications.

questions.question: Write three simple Sanskrit sentences (2-3 lines) in Devanagari about the value of hard work (उद्यमः). Give their English meaning.
questions.answer:
1. उद्यमेन कार्याणि सिध्यन्ति। (Tasks are accomplished by effort.)
2. आलस्यं महान् रिपुः अस्ति। (Laziness is a great enemy.)
3. छात्रः नित्यम् उद्यमं करोति। (The student does effort/works hard every day.)
Together these say: we should work hard, avoid laziness, and act daily — because effort, not wishing, brings success.
questions.explanation: Simple प्रथमा-subject sentences using vocabulary from the chapter; verbs सिध्यन्ति, अस्ति, करोति.

questions.question: Translate: 'परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः परोपकाराय वहन्ति नद्यः' and state its moral.
questions.answer: Translation: Trees (वृक्षाः) bear fruit for the good of others (परोपकाराय); rivers (नद्यः) flow for the good of others. Moral: Nature itself lives to serve others, so human beings too should live for परोपकार — helping and serving others.
questions.explanation: परोपकाराय = dative 'for the benefit of others'; the verse models selfless service.

questions.question: Read: 'काकः कृष्णः पिकः कृष्णः को भेदः पिककाकयोः'. Why does the poet say the crow and the koel look the same, and when is the difference revealed?
questions.answer: Both the crow (काकः) and the koel (पिकः) are black (कृष्णः), so by appearance there seems to be no difference (को भेदः). The real difference is revealed when spring (वसन्त) arrives — then the koel's sweet song shows its true worth, while the crow only caws. Appearance is not the same as true worth.
questions.explanation: The verse teaches that inner quality, not outward look, is revealed at the right time.

questions.question: What is a सुभाषितम्, and give two reasons why subhashitas are valued.
questions.answer: A सुभाषितम् is a 'well-said' verse (सु + भाषितम्) — a short, memorable Sanskrit श्लोक that carries a moral or piece of worldly wisdom. Two reasons they are valued: (1) they teach values and good conduct in an easy-to-remember form; (2) being short and rhythmic, they also help learners pick up vocabulary, सन्धि and grammar naturally.
questions.explanation: Definition (सु + भाषितम्) plus its educational and moral value.

What does the word 'सुभाषितम्' literally mean, and what kind of composition is it?
questions.answer: सुभाषितम् literally means a 'well-said (thing)' — सु (well/good) + भाषितम् (spoken). It is a short, memorable Sanskrit verse (a श्लोक) that carries a moral teaching or piece of worldly wisdom.

questions.question: Give two reasons why subhashitas are important in learning Sanskrit.
questions.answer: (1) They are short and rhythmic, so they are easy to memorise and teach values and good conduct. (2) While memorising them, a learner naturally picks up vocabulary, सन्धि and विभक्ति, so they double as a grammar and vocabulary aid.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of 'विद्या ददाति विनयम्' in one sentence.
questions.answer: It means 'knowledge (विद्या) gives (ददाति) humility (विनयम्)' — that is, true learning makes a person humble and well-behaved.

questions.question: Explain the message of the verse 'काकः कृष्णः पिकः कृष्णः...'.
questions.answer: Both the crow (काक) and the koel (पिक) are black (कृष्ण), so by appearance there is no visible difference (को भेदः). But when spring (वसन्त) comes, the koel's sweet song reveals its true worth while the crow only caws. The message: outward looks can be alike; real worth is shown at the right time.
questions.explanation: Appearance vs true worth, revealed in season.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: सिंहस्य, मुखे, मृगाः.
questions.answer: सिंहस्य = of the lion; मुखे = in the mouth; मृगाः = deer (plural).
questions.explanation: Word meanings from the sleeping-lion verse.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: सत्यम्, प्रियम्, अनृतम्.
questions.answer: सत्यम् = truth; प्रियम् = pleasant/agreeable; अनृतम् = falsehood/untruth.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: वृक्षाः, नद्यः, गावः.
questions.answer: वृक्षाः = trees; नद्यः = rivers; गावः = cows (all nominative plural).

questions.question: State and briefly explain the moral of 'आलस्यं हि मनुष्याणां शरीरस्थो महान् रिपुः'.
questions.answer: The moral is that laziness (आलस्य) is a great enemy (महान् रिपु) that lives within our own body, while diligence/effort (उद्यम) is our truest friend (बन्धु). We should conquer laziness and work hard, for one who cultivates उद्यम never sinks into ruin (न अवसीदति).

questions.question: What lesson does the sun-simile in 'उदये सविता रक्तो रक्तश्चास्तमये तथा' teach?
questions.answer: Just as the sun is equally red at sunrise and sunset, great souls (महात्) keep the same even, calm mind in both prosperity (सम्पत्ति) and adversity (विपत्ति). The lesson is steadiness of character in all circumstances.

questions.question: 'A friend asks you to tell a lie so he feels happy.' Using verse 5, explain what you should do.
questions.answer: Verse 5 says: सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात्... प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात् — speak the truth and speak pleasantly, but do not speak even a pleasant falsehood. So I should not tell the lie; instead I should tell the truth in a gentle, kind way that does not hurt him. Truth must be preserved, and kindness lies in HOW it is said, not in replacing it with a lie.
questions.explanation: Applies 'no pleasant lie'; truth told kindly.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'परोपकाराय वहन्ति नद्यः'.
questions.answer: 'Rivers flow for the good of others' — नद्यः (rivers) वहन्ति (flow) परोपकाराय (for the benefit of others).

questions.question: Translate the full verse 'विद्या ददाति विनयं विनयाद्याति पात्रताम्, पात्रत्वात् धनमाप्नोति धनात् धर्मं ततः सुखम्'.
questions.answer: Knowledge gives humility; from humility one attains worthiness; from worthiness one obtains wealth; from wealth one performs righteous duty (धर्म); and from that comes happiness (सुख). It shows a step-by-step ladder from learning to happiness.

questions.question: Translate 'उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः' and name the moral in one phrase.
questions.answer: 'Tasks are accomplished by effort (उद्यमेन), not by mere wishes (मनोरथैः).' Moral in one phrase: hard work brings success.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) धनमाप्नोति (b) कणशश्च.
questions.answer: (a) धनमाप्नोति = धनम् + आप्नोति. (b) कणशश्च = कणशः + च (visarga ः → श् before च).

questions.question: Join by sandhi: (a) न + अवसीदति (b) विद्या + अर्थी.
questions.answer: (a) न + अवसीदति = नावसीदति (अ + अ = आ). (b) विद्या + अर्थी = विद्यार्थी (आ + अ = आ).

questions.question: What is दीर्घ-सन्धि? Give one example from the verses.
questions.answer: दीर्घ-सन्धि is the rule by which a short vowel meeting a similar vowel merges into a single long vowel. Example: न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ + अ = आ).

questions.question: Give the विभक्ति (case) and role of: (a) मनोरथैः (b) सिंहस्य.
questions.answer: (a) मनोरथैः = तृतीया (instrumental), plural — 'by wishes'. (b) सिंहस्य = षष्ठी (genitive), singular — 'of the lion'.

questions.question: Write the शब्दरूप of राम in प्रथमा विभक्ति (all three numbers).
questions.answer: प्रथमा: एकवचन रामः, द्विवचन रामौ, बहुवचन रामाः.

questions.question: Which विभक्ति do the endings '-आत्' and '-ए' usually mark? Give the English sense of each.
questions.answer: '-आत्' marks पञ्चमी (ablative), meaning 'from' (e.g. विनयात् = from humility). '-ए' marks सप्तमी (locative), meaning 'in/at/on' (e.g. मुखे = in the mouth).

questions.question: Explain the meaning of 'नास्त्युद्यमसमो बन्धुः'.
questions.answer: It means 'there is no friend (बन्धु) equal to industry/effort (उद्यम)'. Diligence is described as our best friend, because one who works hard never falls into ruin.

questions.question: Which subhashita would you quote to a friend who wastes time, and why?
questions.answer: I would quote 'क्षणशः कणशश्चैव विद्यामर्थं च साधयेत्; क्षणे नष्टे कुतो विद्या...'. It teaches that knowledge and wealth are built moment by moment, and that a wasted moment means lost learning — so time should never be wasted.

questions.question: What is a सुभाषितम्? Explain its meaning, form and importance in Sanskrit literature.
questions.answer:
A सुभाषितम् is a 'well-said saying', formed from सु (well/good) and भाषितम् (that which is spoken). In form it is usually a single श्लोक of two lines (four quarters), composed in a pleasing rhythm. Its purpose is to pack a moral teaching or a piece of worldly wisdom into a short, memorable verse.
Subhashitas are important for several reasons: (1) they teach values such as humility, hard work, truthfulness and service in a form that is easy to remember; (2) before printed books, elders and teachers used them as the everyday 'textbook of values'; (3) they delight the ear, sharpen the mind and improve character all at once; and (4) they help students learn Sanskrit vocabulary, सन्धि and विभक्ति naturally while enjoying the verse. For all these reasons subhashitas hold a treasured place in Sanskrit literature.

questions.question: Take the verse 'विद्या ददाति विनयं विनयाद्याति पात्रताम्, पात्रत्वात् धनमाप्नोति धनात् धर्मं ततः सुखम्'. Give its word meanings and full explanation.
questions.answer:
शब्दार्थ: विद्या = knowledge; ददाति = gives; विनयम् = humility; विनयात् = from humility; याति = attains; पात्रताम् = worthiness; पात्रत्वात् = from worthiness; धनम् = wealth; आप्नोति = obtains; धनात् = from wealth; धर्मम् = righteous duty; ततः = from that; सुखम् = happiness.
Explanation: The verse describes a chain (a ladder) of cause and effect. Knowledge first gives a person humility and good conduct. Humility earns worthiness or fitness (people trust and respect a humble learned person). Worthiness leads to the honest gaining of wealth. Wealth, rightly used, enables one to perform धर्म (righteous duties and charity). And righteous living finally brings true happiness (सुख). The verse thus teaches that real education is not just information but the beginning of a whole path of character that ends in happiness.

questions.question: Discuss the theme of परोपकार using the verse 'परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः...' and explain how one can practise it in daily life.
questions.answer:
The verse says: trees (वृक्षाः) bear fruit for others, rivers (नद्यः) flow for others, cows (गावः) give milk for others — and this body (शरीर) too is meant for helping others (परोपकार). The poet points to nature as a teacher: none of these serve themselves; a tree does not eat its own fruit, a river does not drink its own water. The theme is that the true purpose of life is service to others.
In daily life a student can practise परोपकार by helping classmates with studies, sharing books, caring for parents and elders, being kind to animals, keeping public places clean, and volunteering for the needy. Even small acts of unselfish help fulfil the verse's teaching. By living for others we make our own life meaningful, just as nature does.
questions.explanation: Explains the verse and gives practical परोपकार.

questions.question: Write any TWO subhashitas from the lesson in Devanagari and state the moral of each.
questions.answer:
1. उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः। न हि सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य प्रविशन्ति मुखे मृगाः॥ — Moral: hard work, not mere wishing, brings success; even a lion must make effort.
2. सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात् न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम्। प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात् एष धर्मः सनातनः॥ — Moral: always speak the truth, but speak it kindly; never a harsh truth nor a pleasant lie.
questions.explanation: Recall of two verses + their morals.

questions.question: Compare the ideas of आलस्य (laziness) and उद्यम (effort) as taught in the subhashitas.
questions.answer: The subhashitas treat आलस्य and उद्यम as opposites. 'आलस्यं हि मनुष्याणां शरीरस्थो महान् रिपुः' calls laziness a great enemy that lives inside our own body — it holds us back from every good thing. In the same verse, 'नास्त्युद्यमसमो बन्धुः' praises effort as our best friend, because 'कृत्वा यं नावसीदति' — cultivating it, one never sinks into ruin. The verse 'उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः' adds that tasks are achieved only by उद्यम, not by day-dreaming (मनोरथ), just as deer do not enter a sleeping lion's mouth. Together the verses teach us to defeat the inner enemy आलस्य and befriend उद्यम to succeed in life.
questions.explanation: Contrast using two verses; enemy vs friend.

questions.question: Translate the verse 'अयं निजः परो वेति गणना लघुचेतसाम्, उदारचरितानां तु वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम्' and explain it.
questions.answer:
Translation: '"This one is my own (निजः), that one is a stranger (परः)" — such reckoning belongs to the narrow-minded (लघुचेतस्); but for the noble-hearted (उदारचरित), the whole earth (वसुधा) itself is one family (कुटुम्बकम्).'
Explanation: The verse contrasts two mindsets. Small-minded people constantly divide the world into 'mine' and 'other' and act selfishly. Broad-minded, generous people rise above such divisions and treat all human beings as members of one family. The famous phrase वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम् has become India's great message of universal brotherhood and harmony.

questions.question: Explain सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद with four examples taken from the verses of this chapter.
questions.answer:
सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; सन्धि-विच्छेद is splitting such a joined form back into its separate words. Examples from the verses:
1. न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
2. विद्या + अर्थी = विद्यार्थी (आ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
3. वसुधा + एव = वसुधैव (आ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धि-सन्धि).
4. विनयात् + याति = विनयाद्याति (त् → द् before य, व्यञ्जन-सन्धि).
Being able to both join (सन्धि) and split (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is essential for reading Sanskrit verses correctly.
questions.explanation: Definition + four worked examples with rules.

questions.question: Explain the six common विभक्ति (cases) with one example each drawn from the verses.
questions.answer:
Sanskrit nouns change their ending to show their role:
1. प्रथमा (nominative, subject): सविता 'the sun', वृक्षाः 'trees'.
2. द्वितीया (accusative, object): विनयम् 'humility (as object)', विद्याम् 'knowledge'.
3. तृतीया (instrumental, 'by/with'): उद्यमेन 'by effort', मनोरथैः 'by wishes'.
4. पञ्चमी (ablative, 'from'): विनयात् 'from humility', धनात् 'from wealth'.
5. षष्ठी (genitive, 'of'): सिंहस्य 'of the lion', महताम् 'of the great'.
6. सप्तमी (locative, 'in/at'): मुखे 'in the mouth', वसन्तसमये 'in spring'.
Recognising these endings helps us understand who does what in a verse.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer the questions:
उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः।
न हि सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य प्रविशन्ति मुखे मृगाः॥
(a) By what are tasks accomplished? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'मनोरथैः'. (c) In which विभक्ति is 'सिंहस्य'? (d) State the moral.
questions.answer: (a) Tasks (कार्याणि) are accomplished by effort (उद्यमेन), not by wishes. (b) मनोरथैः = 'by (mere) wishes/day-dreams' (instrumental plural). (c) सिंहस्य is षष्ठी (genitive) — 'of the lion'. (d) Moral: hard work, not day-dreaming, brings success; even a lion must make effort to eat.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: meaning, word, case and moral.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
विद्या ददाति विनयं विनयाद्याति पात्रताम्।
पात्रत्वात् धनमाप्नोति धनात् धर्मं ततः सुखम्॥
(a) What does knowledge give first? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'सुखम्'. (c) Split by सन्धि-विच्छेद: 'धनमाप्नोति'. (d) What is the overall message?
questions.answer: (a) Knowledge first gives विनय (humility). (b) सुखम् = happiness. (c) धनमाप्नोति = धनम् + आप्नोति. (d) Message: education is a ladder from humility through worthiness, wealth and righteous duty, finally to happiness.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
अयं निजः परो वेति गणना लघुचेतसाम्।
उदारचरितानां तु वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम्॥
(a) Who makes the 'mine vs other' reckoning? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'वसुधा'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'वसुधैव'. (d) What value does the verse teach?
questions.answer: (a) The narrow-minded (लघुचेतस्) make the 'mine (निजः) vs other (परः)' reckoning. (b) वसुधा = the earth. (c) वसुधैव = वसुधा + एव. (d) Value: universal brotherhood — the noble treat the whole world as one family (वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम्).
questions.explanation: Comprehension: theme, word, sandhi split, value.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात् न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम्।
प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात् एष धर्मः सनातनः॥
(a) What two qualities should speech have? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'अनृतम्'. (c) What does the verb 'ब्रूयात्' mean? (d) What is the moral?
questions.answer: (a) Speech should be truthful (सत्य) and pleasant/kind (प्रिय). (b) अनृतम् = falsehood/untruth. (c) ब्रूयात् = 'one should speak'. (d) Moral: speak truth kindly — never a harsh truth nor a pleasant lie; this is the eternal (सनातन) law.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
काकः कृष्णः पिकः कृष्णः को भेदः पिककाकयोः।
वसन्तसमये प्राप्ते काकः काकः पिकः पिकः॥
(a) What colour are both birds? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'भेदः'. (c) When is the difference revealed? (d) What is the lesson?
questions.answer: (a) Both are black (कृष्ण). (b) भेदः = difference. (c) The difference is revealed when spring (वसन्त) arrives — the koel sings sweetly. (d) Lesson: outward appearance may be alike; true worth is shown at the right time.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः परोपकाराय वहन्ति नद्यः।
परोपकाराय दुहन्ति गावः परोपकारार्थमिदं शरीरम्॥
(a) Why do trees bear fruit? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'गावः'. (c) Translate 'परोपकाराय वहन्ति नद्यः'. (d) What is the central theme?
questions.answer: (a) Trees bear fruit for the good of others (परोपकाराय). (b) गावः = cows. (c) 'Rivers flow for the good of others.' (d) Central theme: परोपकार — service to others is the very purpose of life.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
आलस्यं हि मनुष्याणां शरीरस्थो महान् रिपुः।
नास्त्युद्यमसमो बन्धुः कृत्वा यं नावसीदति॥
(a) What is called a great enemy? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'बन्धुः'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'नास्ति'. (d) What is the moral?
questions.answer: (a) Laziness (आलस्य) is called the great enemy dwelling in the body. (b) बन्धुः = friend/kinsman. (c) नास्ति = न + अस्ति. (d) Moral: conquer laziness and befriend उद्यम (effort), for one who works hard never sinks into ruin.
questions.explanation: Comprehension with sandhi split; enemy vs friend.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
उदये सविता रक्तो रक्तश्चास्तमये तथा।
सम्पत्तौ च विपत्तौ च महतामेकरूपता॥
(a) To what is a great soul compared? (b) In which विभक्ति are 'सम्पत्तौ' and 'विपत्तौ'? (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'एकरूपता'. (d) What is the message?
questions.answer: (a) A great soul is compared to the sun (सविता), red at both rising and setting. (b) सम्पत्तौ and विपत्तौ are सप्तमी (locative) — 'in prosperity', 'in adversity'. (c) एकरूपता = sameness / evenness (of temper). (d) Message: great souls keep an even, calm mind in both good and bad times.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
क्षणशः कणशश्चैव विद्यामर्थं च साधयेत्।
क्षणे नष्टे कुतो विद्या कणे नष्टे कुतो धनम्॥
(a) How should one gather knowledge? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'साधयेत्'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'कणशश्च'. (d) What is the moral?
questions.answer: (a) One should gather knowledge moment by moment (क्षणशः) and wealth particle by particle (कणशः). (b) साधयेत् = 'one should acquire/accomplish'. (c) कणशश्च = कणशः + च. (d) Moral: waste neither time nor resources; small steady efforts build learning and wealth.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
पुस्तकस्था तु या विद्या परहस्तगतं धनम्।
कार्यकाले समुत्पन्ने न सा विद्या न तद्धनम्॥
(a) What two things are compared? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'कार्यकाले'. (c) In which विभक्ति is 'कार्यकाले'? (d) What is the lesson?
questions.answer: (a) Knowledge left only in a book (पुस्तकस्था विद्या) is compared with wealth gone into another's hand (परहस्तगतं धनम्). (b) कार्यकाले = 'at the time of need/work'. (c) कार्यकाले is सप्तमी (locative). (d) Lesson: knowledge must be learnt and usable; knowledge stuck only in books is of no use in the hour of need.
